title: Clarify intake requirements: versioning semantics and runtime compatibility notes for new open-model entries
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Problem: Our current open-model intake flow accepts a wide variety of community-submitted variants without a consistent contract for version semantics or runtime compatibility notes. This causes ambiguity for runtime routing, fallback pins, and customer expectations when a model variant behaves differently across hardware/quantization modes. Goal: Produce a clarified, actionable set of intake requirements and acceptance criteria that product, eng, and onboarding engineers can apply to new open-model submissions to ensure predictable serving behavior and clear pinning guidance.
background: We observe three recurring failure patterns: 1) community variants lacking any versioning semantics (no semver or changelog) leading to silent behavior changes; 2) missing runtime compatibility notes (seq-len, kv-cache requirements, attention-opts), resulting in runtime misconfiguration or suboptimal kernel selection; 3) ambiguous fallback/pinning rules for models with multiple quantized artifacts or fused kernels. Current intake PRD drafts include soft-pinning and compat tags, but we lack a concise acceptance checklist that feeds both catalog metadata and the runtime admission control.
scope_changes: This ticket narrows earlier PRD scope to focus only on 'intake metadata contract' and 'compatibility note taxonomy' for open models. It deliberately excludes automated runtime pipeline changes (ENG work) and UI listing changes — those will be separate follow-ups. Deliverable is a product-ready requirements doc and a short spec for engineering to implement the metadata validation and admission messaging.
requirements: 1) Every new open-model submission must include: canonical version id, optional upstream commit/hash, human-readable changelog string, and explicit compatibility tags (max-seq-length, kv-cache-hotstart, fused-kernel-expected, dynamic-rope).
acceptance_criteria:
- A concise intake template is approved by PM + Runtime Eng that lists the required metadata fields and optional diagnostic artifacts.
- The template includes a taxonomy of compatibility tags (at least these: 'seq:128/512/2048', 'kv-cache:required/optional', 'kernels:default/fused/experimental').
- For models that provide multiple artifacts (fp32, int8/q4, fused kernels), submitter must declare 'primary-serving-artifact' and recommended 'fallback-order' for runtime use.
- A one-page README example is attached for vendors showing how to declare a breaking change vs non-breaking metadata update.
- The admission control spec defines a rejection class for submissions missing the three mandatory items (version id, changelog, compatibility tags).
- Acceptance criteria are reflected in a new intake checklist in Confluence and a short webhook payload spec for the ingestion API.
success_metrics:
- Reduction in runtime incompatibility incidents traced to new-model ingestion by 75% in the first 90 days after rollout.
- 95% of new community-model submissions include both version id and compatibility tags at first submission.
- Mean time to diagnose serving regressions caused by model-variant mismatches reduced from 18h to under 4h by improved metadata clarity.
implementation_todo:
1) Draft intake template and compatibility taxonomy (PM) — this ticket.
2) Hand off JSON schema + webhook field list to Eng (dependency ENG-2412).
3) Create a short onboarding sample guide and two example submissions (one trivial, one multi-artifact).
4) Coordinate a 30-min cross-functional review with Runtime Eng, Catalog Owners, and Onboarding SRE.
5) Publish Confluence intake page and update ingestion API docs.
review_checklist:
- PM sign-off on metadata fields and human-readable examples.
- Runtime Eng validates that declared tags map to kernel/runtime flags.
- Onboarding SRE confirms required artifacts are sufficient for automated sanity runs.
- Legal/security quick-check for external weight provenance guidance.
- UX note for the catalog UI team indicating how 'compatibility tags' should surface.
decisions_log:
- 2026-03-11: Decided not to mandate semver for community models; instead require a stable 'version id' and an explicit changelog entry.
- 2026-03-12: Agreed to standardize compatibility tags rather than free-text notes. A taxonomy was proposed and iterated with Runtime Eng.
- 2026-03-13: Chose to require 'primary-serving-artifact' for multi-artifact submissions; fallback order optional but recommended.
notes:
Partial trade-offs and open questions: should we require checksum validation for artifacts (security/infra cost)? For now mark as 'investigate' and schedule in separate security ticket. We also debated mandatory perf bench outputs — decided to capture as optional 'profiling.csv' in intake.
Feedback from runtime lead: tags must be machine-parseable and limited to a controlled vocabulary to avoid divergent behavior.
Follow-ups: create ENG ticket to wire the webhook rejection codes and intake schema enforcement.
